speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Brethren. A precept from Crosby Place, to be read upon this Sunday. I read it as it was sent.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: No blue starch in ruffs. Starch, brethren. Blue starch. Consider the lilies: they toil not, neither do they starch.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: The daughters of Zion, and their round tires like the moon. Vanity in Isaiah. A collar is a small field, and they have cropped it for colour.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Ten yards. White as a christening. The neck has not moved.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Hush. If you must count, count without a voice.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Vanity in the Epistles also. A city may go hungry and still boil good wheat into a band. The Mayor has said no.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Blue. She has taken a great interest in the beams.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Mine is white. I washed it on Wednesday, as I was bid.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then you are inside the precept. Sit still, and let the white be white.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Let every man see his own band before he sees his neighbour's. We shall be brief, brethren.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: That is once.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I can hear a glass without a clerk.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: The wheat in a collar is the wheat that is not in a loaf. Mark that. The precept is not a riddle, and I am not a riddler.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am counting pews. And heads. And one neck.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: If the blue is washed out, is the starch still the thing he named?

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The pulpit is not a washtub. You were told to wash it. You washed it.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: An offence is what the precept names. A permitted shade is what it leaves alone. I have not come to the parts.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Twice.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: And the text is not spent. Round tires, and cauls, and the changeable suits. I have the chapter in front of me, and I mean to use it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Do not grin at a chapter.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not grinning. I am still counting.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: Then count the vanity, and leave my glass to finish its own work.

speaker: josias_thwaite
text: The precept is read. I have not finished the text, and I did not say that I had.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then I will sit until you finish it. I have already counted two turns.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Sit. The next turn of the glass is his work, not your announcement.
